newsitem.title: UK: Brent weakens on ample supply in slow N.Sea trade.
newsitem.headline: Brent weakens on ample supply in slow N.Sea trade.

text.p: The value of Brent Blend slid on the North Sea spot market on Wednesday under pressure from ample demand and little interest for late March barrels, with a cargo changing hands 13 cents under the original offer, traders said.

The cargo sold at April Brent minus eight cents, sharply down from the April +12 cents on a March 15-17 loader on Tuesday. The cargo, originally offered at April +5 cents, was one of two March 19-21 loaders shown to the market on Wednesday.
"We are already talking late March and most of the requirements are covered," a broker said. "Everyone knows that there will be more barrels available."
Further pressure came from the closure of the U.S. arb.

Trader said cargoes for later dates were already offered at a discount of over 10 cents to April Brent. They added that the support derived by prompt cargoes from Glencore's buying last week and from loading delays was starting to wear off.
The outright price also came off. The front month April contract for IPE Brent futures was down 25 cents at $19.25 a barrel, 10 cents off the day's low, at 1853 GMT.
J Aron kept the sole Brent nominated from the paper chains. The cargo loads March 20-22.
A Statfjord loading March 26-28 sold at Dated +35 cents.
That was down three cents from the level achieved by March 22-24 and 23-25 loaders Monday.
A European major offered a Forties loading March 29-31 at Dated Brent +45, three cents up on the level agreed for a March 27-29 loader on Monday.
Intermonth spreads were mixed. April/May weakened to trade twice at +30 cents from talk earlier at +37/38 cents. March/April paper was talked down at +15/+18 cents from +21/+25.
CFDs were mainly weak and moderately traded. March 10-14 softened to around April -14/-11 cents, down from -10/-5 cents. March 17-21 was April -16/-14 cents, up from -19/-16 cents.
